findings.title: D9 and §7.3 describe makedocs as erroring on any gate failure; the code silently skips the build instead when a docs round is open
locations: docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:483-488 — "gate(\"check-docs\", \"check-consistency\") **in-process** before Documenter ... `error()`s on any non-zero return, so the gate is reachable on a CI runner with no shim"

docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:1777 — `WIRE.MAKEDOCS` row: "calls `GBGCodingTools.makedocs(` and contains no `makedocs(` token not preceded by `GBGCodingTools.` and no `function lint_`" (no mention of the deploydocs guard clause)
findings.contradicts: ext/GBGCodingToolsDocumenterExt.jl:24-31 — "if code == 1 && !isempty(frozen) && !haskey(ENV, \"GBG_DOCS_NO_SKIP\") ... println(\"makedocs: SKIPPED — \", ...); return nothing end"; src/CLI/Doctor.jl:381-386 — the WIRE.MAKEDOCS check also fails on an unconditional `deploydocs(` because "the wrapper returns nothing when a round froze the build"
findings.description: D9 states the makedocs wrapper `error()`s on any non-zero return from `gate("check-docs", "check-consistency")`, and calls this the tool's 'per-push, harness-independent enforcement point' precisely because every push runs it. But the actual `ext/GBGCodingToolsDocumenterExt.jl` body has a documented exception: when the gate returns 1 because a docs-instrument round is open (RULE.INST.FROZEN_MIDROUND), it does NOT error — it prints a 'SKIPPED' line and returns `nothing` without ever calling `Documenter.makedocs`, exiting 0, unless the environment variable `GBG_DOCS_NO_SKIP` is set (which only `gbg release` and the deep doctor set). This is not a stray implementation detail: it is load-bearing enough that a second doctor check, `WIRE.MAKEDOCS`, was extended to fail on an unconditional `deploydocs(` call specifically because 'the wrapper returns nothing when a round froze the build' (src/CLI/Doctor.jl comment). The `makedocs` docstring in src/DocLints.jl documents this skip behaviour clearly and accurately, so the feature is real and current — but ARCHITECTURE.md, whose purpose is exactly to record such design decisions with their 'forced by' rationale, never mentions it anywhere (no revision entry references `GBG_DOCS_NO_SKIP`, 'SKIPPED', or 'frozen' in this sense outside of D10/D13's round-freeze vocabulary). A reader relying on D9's account would wrongly conclude that `docs.yml` fails loudly on every push while a `/check-docs` or `/check-consistency` round is open, when it actually degrades to a silent no-op build (exit 0) — the opposite of what 'per-push, harness-independent enforcement point' promises.
findings.resolution_hint: Add a clause to D9's makedocs bullet (and to the §7.3 WIRE.MAKEDOCS row) stating the frozen-round exception: makedocs returns `nothing` and prints a SKIPPED line instead of erroring when `frozen_rounds` reports an open docs-instrument round, unless `GBG_DOCS_NO_SKIP` is set (as `gbg release` and the deep doctor do); cross-reference `Gate.frozen_rounds`'s own docstring, which already states the rationale precisely.

findings.title: D5's list of supported JSON-Schema-subset keywords omits minLength/minimum/maximum, which Schema.jl already validates
locations: docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:334-336 — "the JSON-Schema-subset validator (types, `required`, `enum`, `pattern`, `additionalProperties`, nested objects and arrays)"
docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:962 — "the ONE JSON-Schema-subset validator (types, required, enum, pattern, additionalProperties)"
findings.contradicts: src/CLI/Schema.jl:107-117 — the validator also checks `minLength` (line 113-114), `minimum` (line 116) and `maximum` (line 117) in addition to type/enum/pattern/additionalProperties
findings.description: RULE.DOC.CURRENT says a summary naming only a subset of what the code now provides is stale even if every listed item is literally true. D5's two enumerations of Schema.jl's supported keywords (repeated near-verbatim at two places in the document) both omit `minLength`, `minimum` and `maximum`, which src/CLI/Schema.jl's `validate()` function implements alongside the listed keywords. This is a minor completeness gap rather than a behavioural contradiction, but it is the kind of stale enumerated list the doc-edit checklist's currency item exists to catch, and it recurs at two locations (a small class).
findings.resolution_hint: Extend both enumerations to "(types, `required`, `enum`, `pattern`, `minLength`, `minimum`, `maximum`, `additionalProperties`, nested objects and arrays)" so the parenthetical is exhaustive rather than illustrative, or explicitly mark it as illustrative if that is the intent.
